key_insight: A two-level machine-learning framework can map phase stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloys, showing that stable regions are narrow and strongest at high iodine content.
engineering_relevance: The results help narrow the composition space for designing more stable Pb- and especially Sn-based perovskite solar absorbers.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data for fast structure relaxation
Secondary ML models to predict energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures
Free-energy calculations across composition and phase space, including alloy disorder and FA molecular orientations
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3 alloys and produced free-energy phase landscapes that distinguish their stability regions.
watch_item: Because the workflow relies on stacked ML models and detailed alloy sampling, accuracy may depend on coverage of the training data and transferability across compositions.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
